A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same QSD-Transformer work. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and Appendices A–G are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification, detection, segmentation, transfer-learning and ablation results in Section 5, Tables 1–6, and qualitative examples in Figures 4–5.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results, including the benchmark comparisons, component ablations and appendix visualizations.

M1.justification: The quantization procedure, IE-LIF neuron, membrane-potential rectification, fine-grained distillation loss and training-to-inference conversion remain unchanged in Sections 3–4.

E1.justification: Both versions use ImageNet-1K classification, COCO detection, ADE20K segmentation, and transfer learning on CIFAR10, CIFAR100 and CIFAR10-DVS. No dataset, task or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within Tables 1–5, including the ImageNet baselines, detection and segmentation comparators, Spikformer and SpikingResformer transfer comparisons, and architecture-specific ablations.

E3.justification: Section 5 and Appendix G retain the same splits, preprocessing, metrics, model configurations and training schedules, including 300-epoch ImageNet training and 24-epoch COCO fine-tuning.

E4.justification: Figures 2–3 retain the quantization-sensitivity and attention-distribution analyses. Tables 5–6 retain the component, weight-bit, activity-bit and timestep ablations, and Figures 4–5 show the same qualitative examples.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five transfer-learning repetitions with different random seeds and report the same ± uncertainty entries in Table 4. No statistical reporting practice is added or revised.

E6.justification: The numerical results and qualitative findings are unchanged. Corresponding entries retain 80.3% ImageNet accuracy, 57.0% COCO mAP@0.5 and 40.5% ADE20K MIoU; transfer-learning scores, ablation results and plotted findings also match.

T1.justification: The definitions, propositions, proofs and derivations remain unchanged. Appendix A, Equation 15, changes an isolated uppercase W to lowercase w to match the existing weight notation; this does not revise the mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about spike information distortion, bi-level optimization, and accuracy and efficiency across vision tasks. Their scope and strength are unchanged.

C2.justification: The explanations of attention distortion and activity-bit versus timestep effects are retained. Appendix F preserves the same scalability and hardware-deployment limitations, exclusion of memory-access energy, and proposed future validation.

D1.justification: Appendices E and G retain the same energy-estimation procedure, hyperparameters, architecture configurations, preprocessing, GPU hardware and training times. The code link and code/model release statements are also unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works, reference list and research positioning are unchanged, including the relationship to spike-driven Transformer v2 and earlier compression methods. Citation-color changes do not alter attribution.

P1.justification: v4 moves Malu Zhang to second author, expands the funding acknowledgment, abbreviates one 'Figure' reference to 'Fig.', and standardizes the weight symbol in Equation 15. The scientific prose and section organization otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v4 displays citations and cross-references in blue and slightly reflows the acknowledgment/reference page. Figures 1–5 and Tables 1–9 retain their content, structure and placement.

improvement.justification: v4 preserves the scientific evidence, arguments, reproducibility information and limitations of v1. The notation correction, link styling and acknowledgment updates provide small editorial refinements without a meaningful change in overall paper quality.
